scenes.narration: A network might have a hundred devices to watch. You can't walk up to each one. S N M P lets you ask them remotely.

scenes.heading: A gated community
scenes.narration: Think of a gated community with different gate systems. Version two C uses a community string, like a shared password. Version three adds real logins and encryption. Auth priv gives both authentication and encryption. Queries use U D P one sixty one, and traps use one sixty two.

scenes.heading: Versions
scenes.narration: Here's how they compare. Version two C uses a community string, and version three uses a username. Version two C has no encryption, but version three can encrypt. And version three has three security levels.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Auth no priv doesn't encrypt. Community strings are plaintext. Version three uses users, not strings.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Version three is the secure one. Queries use U D P one sixty one, and traps use one sixty two. Community strings are plaintext. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva SNMP lab.
